title: Why Collectors Are Keeping Vintage NBA Cards in 2026
summary: Vintage NBA cards are surging. Discover why basketball card collectors on Courtyard are holding cards from Jordan, Kobe, and Shaq instead of redeeming them.
body_markdown:
Vintage NBA cards have been having a moment in 2026.


First it was[Michael Jordan](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/national-sports-collectors-convention-2026-live-updates/z92yZbK0GoBf/O4PYbUpWFUdJ/) , His Airness, leading a wave of nostalgia-fueled buying. Then, as prices became too much for some, his heir,[Kobe Bryant](https://thecollectornation.com/analysis/the-kobe-1-1m-sale-is-a-hall-of-famer-story-not-a-kobe-story-and-it) , saw increased demand. When the Black Mamba’s cards boomed, others turned to his former running mate,[Shaq](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/why-shaquille-oneal-cards-are-suddenly-the-hottest-ticket-in-the-hobby) , who always[finds a way to offer comfort in times of change](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a0n2lakpxfg) .


As hoop heads clamor to own cardboard from yesteryear, **the same trend has emerged on Courtyard, where the rate of collectors opting to keep pulls of vintage NBA players increased by more than 30% between the first half of 2026 and October of 2026** .


As Kevin Garnett famously said, “[Anything is possible!](https://www.youtube.com/@espnthrowback/shorts) ”


Defining vintage as cards from 1980-2005 (a number that will undoubtedly make some of us feel old…), we took a look at the choices[basketball card collectors on Courtyard](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BrefinementList%5D%5Bmetadata.Category%5D%5B0%5D=Basketball) have after[ripping a basketball pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=basketball) : keep the card, stashing it in their Courtyard collection where[the graded, authenticated card](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/welcome-to-card-school-the-difference-between-slabbed-cards-and-their-raw-counterparts) is[safely secured inside of a fine-art-grade vault](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/is-courtyard-io-legit-heres-what-you-need-to-know) ; flip it, by accepting Courtyard’s guaranteed buyback offer or listing it on Courtyard’s marketplace where it can be[sold for 0% seller fees](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/11955240-a-guide-to-the-courtyard-marketplace) ; or ship it,[having the card mailed to their home](https://docs.courtyard.io/courtyard/logistics-and-legal/asset-redemption-and-shipping) so they can proudly display it. The data was surprising.


The timing here is worth noting, too:[2026-27 Topps Flagship Basketball](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/2026-27-topps-flagship-basketball-rookies-guide) released on November 5th, 2026. Packed with highly-touted draft picks like AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson, Cameron Boozer, Caleb Wilson, Darius Acuff Jr., and more, the new rookie class has the Hobby’s attention in a chokehold—and yet Courtyard’s data says vintage is holding its own. We dig some digging to find out the reason some collectors are focusing on vintage in spite of such a strong rookie class.


Someone grab the aux and blast “[Roundball Rock](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9qCEX4scaJA) ” immediately. It’s time for buh-buh-buh-buh-buh-basketball!


## **Keep Rates on Courtyard for Vintage NBA Cards Have Climbed Every Month Since July**


Collectors kept a whopping 40% of the vintage NBA cards pulled on Courtyard in October of 2026, up from 13.3% in July of the same year. Through mid-November of this year, the figure has risen still, and is now at 55%.


Further still, redeem rates, which indicate the percentage of vintage NBA collectors that have opted to have a card in their Courtyard collection mailed home to them, fell from 85.5% in July of 2026 to 51.3% in October—which saw nearly triple the number of vintage NBA cards pulled as Courtyard ensured that overall demand for vintage NBA cards was readily available on the platform. Taking this a step further, if you zoom out, October of 2026’s 40% keep rate is above 2025’s 20% and the 27.9% benchmark from the second half of 2024.


Why? While we can't say for sure, there are a few trends working in favor of vintage basketball cards:


- **Nostalgia** : As millenials get older, many have more purchasing power—and as their lives continue to get harder, they're doing whatever they can to[relive their childhood](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/pokemon-cards-value-investors.html) . For many, that means watching[Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) win his six rings with the Bulls.
- **Cost** : While demand has been steadily rising for vintage NBA cards for a while now, many are still far cheaper than their modern counterparts, especially at the lower end. The rising prices of modern boxes, including[the more than 50% increase for 2026-27 Topps Flagship Basketball hobby boxes](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/2026-27-topps-flagship-basketball-rookies-guide) , combined with[NBA fans reminiscing on a time when the three point line wasn't as vital to success](https://sports.yahoo.com/nba-3-point-spree-draws-150000572.html) , has many choosing singles of players from earlier eras of the Association instead of a jumbo, hobby, mega, or blaster.
- **Design:** Whether it was[Panini (allegedly) using AI to write the text on the back of their basketball cards](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7332568/2026/06/04/panini-ai-sports-cards/) , or[Topps getting flak for their artwork](https://www.reddit.com/r/basketballcards/comments/1v94kbg/now_that_topps_have_been_back_a_little_while_in/) , many of which collectors believe rely on AI, basketball fans often reminisce on the high quality imagery found on inserts from the '90s, like Skybox Z Force, Upper Deck Metal Universe, Topps Beam Team, and more.


## **Michael Jordan Cards Lead Basketball Searches on Courtyard**


Basketball collectors have been chasing[Jordan cards](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) for decades, so it’s no surprise that basketball searches on Courtyard have been dominated by MJ. Yet with so much excitement around newer players, the searches for basketball players on Courtyard since June 2026 reveals an interesting trend:


1. [Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)
2. [Kobe Bryant](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kobe%20Bryant&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)
3. [LeBron James](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=LeBron%20James&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)
4. [Cooper Flagg](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cooper%20Flagg&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)
5. [Magic Johnson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Magic%20Johnson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low)


While Kobe managed to flip MJ in October, our larger look at[early-season NBA card demand](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/jordan-kobe-lebron-pace-early-season-nba-card-demand) notes that Jordan remains the top dog—with Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg serving as the only youngster on this list.


As much as modern collectors love[Victor Wembanyama](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Victor%20Wembanyama&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and Flagg, Magic Johnson, who played his last NBA game 30 years ago in 1996, still can’t be denied thanks to his otherworldly run with the Showtime[Lakers](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/all-time-most-valuable-cards-of-lakers-legends-ranked) .


## **Vintage NBA Legends and Modern Superstars Alike Set New Courtyard Marketplace Sales Records**


New releases get all the headlines, but old cards keep turning up where collectors talk.


On the r/basketballcards subreddit, top posts regularly feature old-school players—like this recent post about[a Kevin Garnett refractor card](https://www.reddit.com/r/basketballcards/comments/1xwyjye/old_school_refractor_of_the_big_ticket/) . As demand for vintage NBA cards continues to stay hot, plenty of Basketball Hall of Famers—including the Big Ticket—have set their new all-time sales records on[Courtyard’s peer-to-peer marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BrefinementList%5D%5Bmetadata.Category%5D%5B0%5D=Basketball) since mid-September 2026, led by Magic Johnson’s $2,264 peer-to-peer sale on November 4th.


- **$2,264:**[Magic Johnson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Magic%20Johnson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **– 1980 Topps #6 Bird/Magic/Erving Scoring Leader (PSA 7), up from $494**
- **$1,500:**[Shaquille O'Neal](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Shaquille%20O%27Neal&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **– 1993 Ultra Scoring Kings #8 (BGS 9), up from $1,495**
- **$969.69:**[Allen Iverson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Allen%20Iverson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **– 1997 Ultra Star Power Supreme #2 (PSA 8), up from $450**
- **$800:**[Scottie Pippen](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Scottie%20Pippen&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **– 1996 Topps Chrome Refractor (PSA 9), up from $200**
- **$580:**[Kevin Garnett](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kevin%20Garnett&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **– 1995 Topps Gallery #41 (PSA 10), up from $404**


While the KG sale noted above is a 40% increase over the previous record, Magic, Pippen, and Iverson each *doubled* their previous records. In true Showtime fashion, Magic’s new mark more than 4x’ed his old one.


However, when looking at the all-time greatest sales of vintage NBA cards on Courtyard’s peer-to-peer marketplace, the bar is set much higher:[Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) sits at the top of the list with a $25,000 sale for a 1984 Star #101 (BGS 4.5). It also tops the all-time list for a basketball card on Courtyard’s marketplace. Go figure, MJ stands alone. His Airness is then followed by[Tim Duncan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Tim%20Duncan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) at $10,000 for a 1997 Skybox Premium Star Rubies (PSA 9), and Kobe at $5,000 for a 1998 Skybox Premium That's Jam (PSA 9). When it comes to the list of the biggest vintage NBA card pulls on Courtyard, the list looks similar:


- **$28,357: Michael Jordan – 1984 Star #101 (BGS 4.5)**
- **$10,702: Tim Duncan – 2001 Topps Pristine Autograph #ATD (BGS 10 PRISTINE)**
- **$8,216:**[Hakeem Olajuwon](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Hakeem%20Olajuwon&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) **– 1986 Fleer Sticker #9 (PSA 10)**


However, modern stars aren’t being left for dead on Courtyard, either.


As[Stephen Curry](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Stephen%20Curry&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) continues through what might be the final season of his career, fans are still chasing cards from the Golden State Warriors guard—and in November 2026, a collector pulled a 2019 Panini Crown Royale Kaboom! #19 Stephen Curry (PSA 10) with a a fair market value (FMV) of $24,175 from a[Basketball Mythic Pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/basketball-mythic-pack) ($5,000). An hour later,[they sold it on the Courtyard marketplace for $24,495](https://www.instagram.com/p/Dfs2_DSDpUV/?hl=en&img_index=1) , with the new owner choosing to redeem the card and have it shipped home shortly after.


It’s not that collectors are choosing vintage over modern, per se, but rather that basketball at large continues to be a category collectors flock to.


## **Why Courtyard is the Place to Chase Vintage NBA Cards**


Some say the NBA season doesn’t start until[the NFL season](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=football) ends. By that metric, fans have a few months to get ahead of NBA All-Star Weekend (February 19th-21st in Phoenix), collecting everything from today’s superstars to the all-time greats of the game. Whether you’re looking to rip a[basketball pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=basketball) or scour the marketplace for cards from[Magic Johnson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Magic%20Johnson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , or[Kobe Bryant](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kobe%20Bryant&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , Courtyard’s got options for every type of hoop head—including those that want to sell their cards without paying pesky sales fees.
